theorem_statement: For every prime p and integer 101<=d<p, a squarefree Z-dependent interpolant A of weighted degree a, with weights (1,1,d), admits an explicit factorwise cleanup. If A=HB, B=c product_i C_i, Delta=wdeg(B), and iota is the weighted degree of gcd(B,B_Z), then at most h+floor((Delta^2-dDelta+(d-1)iota)/d) content or exceptional graph lines are removed. Every remaining separable-type line loses at most min(p,Delta-d) points, every inseparable-type line at most min(p,Delta-1), and every retained point of graph degree at least two satisfies B_Z nonzero. Each irreducible factor has a p-power Hasse height s with weighted degree at least ds, and its height-s stratum obeys the common-graph bound (2r_s-s)Delta_s-d r_s^2. In particular, Delta<pd implies gcd(B,B_Z)=1; if a<=D<pd, at most floor(D^2/d-D) lines and D-d points per remaining line are lost. The threshold pd is sharp: Z^p-XY^(p-1) refutes any lifting rule based solely on multiplicity-weighted direction count. Under the quoted KTZ premise epsilon>=C_KTZ(d/p)^(1/3), the final global agreement remains epsilon/8000.
title: Hasse-Height Stratification and Factorwise Simple-Root Cleanup

theorem_statement: Let p be prime, let 101≤d<p, fix m=2, and use uniform affine point-line sampling. There exist f:F_p²→F_p and degree-exactly-d line labels such that ε=d/p, every affine line has exactly d accepted points, every point has accepted degree d or d+1, exactly pd points have degree d+1, and every line supports acceptance. For every θ∈(0,1], the minimum total nonnegative line weight that gives every accepted incidence θ capped coverage through other accepted lines lies between θp(p+1)/(d+1) and θp(p+1)/(d−1); hence every integral such family has size Ω(p/ε). Nevertheless Q=0 has global agreement one. Moreover, for every valid table of agreement ε, the probability Γ₂ that two uniformly chosen distinct lines through a uniform point both accept there satisfies Γ₂=ε²−ε(1−ε)/p+Var_x(deg_acc(x))/[p(p+1)], and the lower bound is attained by accepting exactly k direction classes, ε=k/(p+1).
title: Sharp Incidence-Only Losses in Bivariate Prime-Field Line–Point Agreement
verified_exponent: No new soundness exponent. The unconditional benchmark remains 1/3; exponents greater than 1/3 would be stronger because 0<d/p<1.

theorem_statement: Fix a prime p, an integer 101<=d<p, and m=2. For every valid table of local agreement epsilon, if a_x and b_L are accepted point and line degrees and J_s is the adjacent-integer interpolation of k↦(k)_s, then Gamma_s^P>=J_s((p+1)epsilon)/(p+1)_s for 0<=s<=p+1 and Gamma_s^L>=J_s(p epsilon)/(p)_s for 0<=s<=p; with-replacement moments are at least epsilon^r. There is an explicit connected legal table at epsilon=d/p attaining both distinct-star envelopes simultaneously for every admissible s, with every line degree d and point degrees d or d+1. For every 0<theta<=1 its fractional other-line reaching optimum lies between theta p(p+1)/(d+1) and theta p(p+1)/(d-1), while Q=0 agrees globally everywhere. Every raw accepted graph is K_{2,2}-free. For the auxiliary line-compatibility graph H, an exact t-th degree-moment DRC bound and a concurrency correction yield at least M_t(H)-binom(t,2)(p+1)/(t-h+1) common-neighbor target lines with h distinct seed intersections.
title: Sharp Higher-Moment Envelopes and Raw-DRC Barriers for Good Affine Incidences

theorem_statement: For C_*=2^60, any nonempty accepted subgraph with point minimum degree u, line minimum degree v, line measure tau, and w=min(u,v), satisfying uv>=C_*dp and uw^2>=C_*d tau p^2, yields one total-degree-at-most-d Q with agreement at least v/(800p). Consequently, if the accepted-edge upper-tail threshold u_* satisfies u_*epsilon^2>=2^70d, then one Q has agreement at least epsilon/12800. The implication is proved, but its improved exponent requires an additional popularity hypothesis not known universally.
title: Popularity-Sensitive Core Decoding and a Bounded-Star-Energy Obstruction
